core.title: Each wagon procedure step declares its pre-conditions and outputs
core.given: A document contains a wagon procedure written as steps
core.when: the step list is written, or any step is added, removed, moved, renumbered or edited
core.then: Every step declares its pre-conditions (what it requires before running) and its outputs (what it produces after).
avoid: Steps whose pre-conditions or outputs are missing or unclear.
core.why: Ordered, numbered steps with pre-conditions and outputs make a wagon procedure reproducible and checkable.
evidence: Reviewer confirms every step declares its pre-conditions.
Reviewer confirms every step declares its outputs.
verification: Severity 2, disposition documentation-only: checked by review; no automated detector is defined.
The requirement is unconditional over change type: no change to a wagon procedure's steps is exempt.
No particular declaration format is required, and a step's pre-conditions need not come from an earlier step's outputs; a check must not flag either.
Scope is the declarations half only: ordering and numbering of the steps are governed by the sibling ordered-numbered rule, not this one.

fires: A new wagon procedure is written as steps.
A step is added, removed or moved.
Step numbers are edited or deleted.
A step's content, pre-conditions or outputs are edited.
doesNotFire: Editing text that contains no wagon procedure steps.
Changing code with no change to any wagon procedure.

neutralityNotes: This is a documentation-authoring convention with no stack mechanics, so the core text mirrors the Bun rewrite almost verbatim. 'Wagon' is retained: it is cross-stack ATDD vocabulary (a bounded slice of the product, cf. layout.wagon_dir and urn.wagon in the closed profile vocabulary), not a stack, runtime or path term. No profile key is needed because the source deliberately does not restrict document type or location, and enforcement is review-based with no detector, validator or finding ids to neutralize. The core activation facts follow the neutral fact schema (fact/values/observability), so the Bun notes were dropped; their substance survives in observability flags, the when clause, the empty unless array and core.verification.
